Actually they imported org.ta4j.core.num.NaN; static import org.ta4j.core.num.NaN.NaN; So they intend to use NaN.NaN maybe. DecimalNum.NaN not defined. Should use NaN.NaN (or just NaN.NaN) for NaN value. So replace DecimalNum.NaN with NaN.NaN (or just NaN). In code: in ArrayIndicator getValue out-of-range return DecimalNum.NaN; change to NaN.NaN.

Also in other places: new ConstantIndicator<>(series, DecimalNum.NaN) replace with NaN.NaN.

- BaseBar constructor: In newer ta4j version, BaseBar expects Duration, ZonedDateTime, Num open, high, low, close, volume maybe. The code uses (ZonedDateTime, double...). Need to use BaseBarBuilder? Simpler: Use new BaseBar(ZonedDateTime, Num open, Num high, Num low, Num close, Num volume). There's a constructor BaseBar(ZonedDateTime time, Num open, Num high, Num low, Num close, Num volume). In the error list constructors show Duration as first param, not ZonedDateTime. There is a constructor with Duration, ZonedDateTime, double,... but not with ZonedDateTime alone. So we need to use BaseBarBuilder or use new BaseBar(Duration.ofSeconds(1), ZonedDateTime..., ...) but we need to supply Duration. Let's use BaseBarBuilder: BaseBar.builder().time(...).open(...).high(...).low(...).close(...).volume(...).build(); However BaseBarBuilder may exist. Simpler: Use new BaseBar(ZonedDateTime.now().plusSeconds(i), numFunction.apply(v), numFunction.apply(v), numFunction.apply(v), numFunction.apply(v), numFunction.apply(0)); but we need a constructor that matches (ZonedDateTime, Num, Num, Num, Num, Num). The error list didn't include that signature, maybe because they have a constructor with Duration first. Let's see constructors list: they show BaseBar.BaseBar(Duration,ZonedDateTime,Function<Number,Num>) etc. So the first argument is Duration (time period). So we can use Duration.ofSeconds(1) as first param. So new BaseBar(Duration.ofSeconds(1), ZonedDateTime.now().plusSeconds(i), v, v, v, v, 0) but types: after Duration and ZonedDateTime, there are double parameters. That matches one constructor: BaseBar(Duration, ZonedDateTime, double open, double high, double low, double close, double volume). So we can pass double values. So modify to new BaseBar(java.time.Duration.ofSeconds(1), ZonedDateTime.now().plusSeconds(i), v, v, v, v, 0.0);

Need import java.time.Duration.

- CrossedUpIndicatorRule getRightIndicator method not found. In ta4j version, CrossedUpIndicatorRule may have methods getLeftIndicator() and getRightIndicator()? maybe not. Let's check: In ta4j core, CrossedUpIndicatorRule extends AbstractRule and has private final Indicator<Num> leftIndicator; private final Indicator<Num> rightIndicator; It may have getter methods getLeftIndicator() and getRightIndicator(). Not sure version. The error indicates method not present. So we need to adjust test to not rely on getRightIndicator. Instead we can just check that rule is instance and that the right indicator value equals constant. Use reflection to access private field or simply evaluate rule.isSatisfied at index 0 maybe. But test expects to verify that the right indicator is ConstantIndicator containing same value. Could replace with: assertTrue(rule.isSatisfied(0) == false) but not verifying. Simpler: remove those assertions and just keep instance check. So modify test method shouldCreateCrossedUpIndicatorRuleWithNumberArgument: after asserting instance, we can get rule's right indicator via reflection if needed. But easier: just assert that rule is instance and that rule.isSatisfied(0) returns false (since crossing not happening). However they also want to assert constant value. Could use reflection to access private field "rightIndicator". Let's implement using reflection: Field field = rule.getClass().getDeclaredField("rightIndicator"); field.setAccessible(true); Indicator<?> right = (Indicator<?>) field.get(rule); assertTrue(right instanceof ConstantIndicator); ConstantIndicator<?> ci = (ConstantIndicator<?>) right; assertEquals(numFunction.apply(constant), ci.getValue(0));

We'll need to import java.lang.reflect.Field.

- Also need to replace @Test annotation import: already imported org.junit.Test (JUnit4). Good.

- Remove static import of NaN.NaN maybe not needed.

- In imports, remove org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension and org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith.

- Also remove @ExtendWith annotation.

- In code, static import of NaN.NaN maybe still fine but we can keep.

- Ensure we have import java.time.Duration.

- Ensure we have import java.lang.reflect.Field.

- Ensure we have import org.ta4j.core.indicators.helpers.ConstantIndicator already there.

- Also the test uses assertThrows defined manually, fine.
